skill.name: freshservice-automation
skill.description: Automate Freshservice ITSM tasks through Rube MCP, including ticket search, ticket creation, bulk updates, service requests, and outbound email tickets.
skill.summary: Guide Freshservice ticket, service request, and outbound email workflows through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static external command, network, and blocker alerts are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and setup documentation. No shell execution, hidden network call, credential access, or reconnaissance behavior is present in SKILL.md. A contextual risk remains because authenticated Freshservice workflows can modify records or send outbound email.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before creating tickets, bulk updating records, creating service requests, or sending outbound email tickets.
Preview ticket IDs and update fields before execution, limit batch size, and report per-ticket success or failure.
Document that users should connect only trusted Freshservice accounts and verify current tool schemas before action workflows.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Freshservice connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `freshservice`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `FRESHSERVICE_LIST_TICKETS` - List tickets with optional filtering and pagination [Required]
2. `FRESHSERVICE_GET_TICKET` - Get detailed information for a specific ticket [Optional]
- `updated_since`: ISO 8601 timestamp to get tickets updated after this time
- Each `include` value consumes additional API credits
- `email`: Requester's email address (provide either email or requester_id)
- Either `email` or `requester_id` must be provided to identify the requester
- `ids`: Array of ticket IDs to update (required)
- `email_config_id`: Email configuration ID for the sender address
- `email_config_id` determines which email address the notification appears to come from
1. `FRESHSERVICE_CREATE_SERVICE_REQUEST` - Create a service request for a catalog item [Required]
- `item_display_id`: Display ID of the catalog item (required)
- `custom_fields`: Custom field values for the service item form
- `parent_ticket_id`: Display ID of a parent ticket (for child requests)
- `item_display_id` can be found in Admin > Service Catalog > item URL (e.g., /service_catalog/items
- Each `include` option consumes additional API credits
- Response data may be nested under `data` or `data.data`
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Ticket IDs can be the internal ID or the display_id shown in the UI
- `email_config_id`: Email configuration ID for the sender address

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Freshservice Actions Require Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to bulk update tickets, create tickets with outbound email, and submit service requests. These legitimate actions can alter ITSM records or notify users if run without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflows explicitly update multiple tickets, create outbound email tickets, and create service requests. The risk is contextual because actions depend on an authenticated Freshservice connection.

content.value_statement: Freshservice teams lose time repeating ticket searches, updates, service requests, and notification steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for consistent ITSM automation.
actual_capabilities: Search and list Freshservice tickets with filters, sorting, pagination, and optional included fields.
Retrieve detailed ticket information by ticket ID or display ID.
Create Freshservice tickets with required subject, description, status, priority, and requester fields.
Bulk update selected tickets with shared field changes after ticket discovery.
Create outbound email tickets and service catalog requests through Freshservice tools.
Explain Freshservice status, priority, pagination, and response parsing patterns.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Freshservice connection before workflows can run.
Tool schemas can change, so the agent must search current tools first.
Freshservice uses numeric status, priority, source, impact, and urgency codes.
Bulk updates apply the same fields to every selected ticket and may partially fail.

use_cases.title: Ticket Queue Review
use_cases.description: Find recent or filtered tickets, review details, and summarize status, priority, requester, and included fields.

use_cases.title: Bulk Ticket Triage
use_cases.description: Identify tickets that need the same update and apply approved status, priority, group, tag, or custom field changes.

use_cases.title: Service Request Intake
use_cases.description: Submit catalog requests, create requester tickets, and prepare outbound email tickets with required Freshservice fields.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: List Freshservice tickets updated since [date]. Include requester details when available and summarize ticket ID, status, priority, and subject.

prompt_templates.title: Create Incident Ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Freshservice incident for [requester email] with subject [subject]. Use priority [priority code] and status [status code]. Confirm before creating.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Bulk Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Find tickets matching [criteria], show the ticket IDs, then ask for approval before applying [update fields] to the selected tickets.

prompt_templates.title: Run Service Request Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for the current Freshservice service request tool schema, create a request for catalog item [item display ID], and report approval status.

output_examples.input: List tickets updated since July 1 and include requester details.
output: Found matching Freshservice tickets across paginated results.
Summarized each ticket by display ID, subject, status, priority, requester, and last updated time.
Noted which records may need follow-up based on priority or age.

output_examples.input: Create an incident for a laptop failure and assign high priority.
output: Prepared the required subject, HTML description, requester email, status code, and priority code.
Asked for confirmation before creating the Freshservice ticket.
Reported the new ticket identifier after creation.

output_examples.input: Bulk update all approved onboarding requests with the same group assignment.
output: Listed the selected ticket IDs and the shared update fields.
Requested approval before running the bulk update.
Summarized successful updates and any per-ticket failures.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP tools before each workflow to confirm current Freshservice schemas.
Confirm ticket IDs, recipients, and update fields before any create, email, or bulk update action.
Use pagination and updated_since filters for complete ticket reviews.
anti_patterns: Running bulk updates without reviewing the selected ticket ID list.
Using string status names when Freshservice requires numeric status and priority codes.
Creating requester records from unverified email addresses.

faq.question: Does this skill require Freshservice credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs an active Freshservice connection through Rube MCP before it can perform account actions.

faq.question: Can it update many tickets at once?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports bulk updates, but users should review ticket IDs and fields before execution.

faq.question: Does it send email?
faq.answer: It can create outbound email tickets when the Freshservice tool is available and the user confirms recipients and content.

faq.question: Why should the agent search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP tool schemas can change. Searching first helps use current parameters and avoid failed calls.

faq.question: Can it retrieve old tickets?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the updated_since filter and pagination because default results may cover only recent tickets.

faq.question: Is it safe for production service desks?
faq.answer: Use it with approval steps, least-privilege Freshservice accounts, and careful review of bulk operations.
